# HTML PPT · 红琥珀警示

A focused entry point into the [`html-ppt`](../html-ppt/SKILL.md) master skill that lands the user directly on the **`testing-safety-alert`** full-deck template.

## When this card is picked

The Examples gallery wires "Use this prompt" to the example_prompt above. When you accept that prompt, this card is the right pick if the user wants exactly the visual identity of `testing-safety-alert` (see the upstream [full-decks catalog](../html-ppt/references/full-decks.md) for screenshots and rationale).

## How to author the deck

1. **Read the master skill first.** All authoring rules live in
   [`skills/html-ppt/SKILL.md`](../html-ppt/SKILL.md) — content/audience checklist,
   token rules, layout reuse, presenter mode, the keyboard runtime, and the
   "never put presenter-only text on the slide" rule.
2. **Start from the matching template folder:**
   `skills/html-ppt/templates/full-decks/testing-safety-alert/` — copy `index.html` and
   `style.css` into the project, keep the `.tpl-testing-safety-alert` body class.
3. **Bring the shared runtime with the template.** The upstream
   `index.html` links the shared CSS/JS via `../../../assets/...` because it
   sits three folders deep inside `skills/html-ppt/templates/full-decks/`.
   Once you copy `index.html` into the project, those parent-relative URLs
   no longer resolve and `base.css`, `animations.css`, and `runtime.js`
   will 404 — meaning the deck never activates and slide navigation is
   dead. Pick one of these two recipes per project:
   - **Recipe A — copy + rewrite (preferred):** copy
     `skills/html-ppt/assets/fonts.css`, `skills/html-ppt/assets/base.css`,
     `skills/html-ppt/assets/animations/animations.css`, and
     `skills/html-ppt/assets/runtime.js` into a project-local
     `assets/` (with `assets/animations/animations.css`), then rewrite the
     four `<link>`/`<script>` tags in `index.html` from
     `../../../assets/...` to the matching project-local paths
     (`assets/fonts.css`, `assets/base.css`,
     `assets/animations/animations.css`, `assets/runtime.js`).
   - **Recipe B — inline:** read the same four files and replace each
     `<link rel="stylesheet" href="../../../assets/...">` with a
     `<style>...</style>` containing the file's contents, and the
     `<script src="../../../assets/runtime.js">` with a
     `<script>...</script>` containing `runtime.js`. Yields a single
     self-contained `index.html`.
   Either way, do not ship the upstream `../../../assets/...` URLs
   verbatim into a project artifact — they only work in-tree.
4. **Pick a theme.** Default tokens look fine; if the user wants a different
   feel, swap in any of the 36 themes from `skills/html-ppt/assets/themes/*.css`
   via `<link id="theme-link">` and let `T` cycle.
5. **Replace demo content, not classes.** The `.tpl-testing-safety-alert` scoped CSS only
   recognises the structural classes shipped in the template — keep them.
6. **Speaker notes go inside `<aside class="notes">` or `<div class="notes">`** — never as visible text on the slide.

## Attribution

Visual system, layouts, themes and the runtime keyboard model come from
the upstream MIT-licensed [`lewislulu/html-ppt-skill`](https://github.com/lewislulu/html-ppt-skill). The
LICENSE file ships at `skills/html-ppt/LICENSE`; please keep it in place when
redistributing.

Open Design · Local Data Safety Brief

Stop sending your designs
to someone else's server
Keep data on your machine

The cost of cloud AI design tools isn't just the subscription — your prompts, design files, brand assets, and API keys all pass through someone else's servers.

Open Design: data never leaves your machine

Sessions, memory, and design artifacts all live in SQLite and the filesystem under your local .od/ directory; API keys stay local and connect straight to the provider.
Apache-2.0 open source · Runs locally · BYOK · No sign-up.

Chapter One

Follow the data

Not every AI design tool treats your data the same way.
First separate "data leaves the machine" from "data stays" — then pick a tool.

section · data flow taxonomy02 / 08
data flow · 3 levels03 / 08

Three flows, three risk profiles

L1 · Green

Local-first

Open Design: designs, memory, and SQLite all live in your local .od/; BYOK connects straight to the provider.
Risk: you're in control

L2 · Amber

Partly in the cloud

Cloud SaaS design tools: files live with the vendor, export formats are limited, and a shutdown cuts you off.
Risk: at the vendor's mercy

L3 · Red

Fully in the cloud

Closed-source cloud AI design: prompts, artifacts, and keys all pass through a third party, model locked to one vendor.
Risk: unauditable

Your API key never leaves your machine

In BYOK mode, keys live only in your local .od/media-config.json, and requests go straight to the model provider — no intermediary servers.

7 questions to ask before you choose a tool

✓
Where do design files live? Can you git diff them? (Open Design: local filesystem)
✓
Does your API key pass through third-party servers? (BYOK: stored locally, direct to provider)
!
Cloud tools: will your prompts and artifacts be used for training? Most terms won't say.
✓
If you go offline or the vendor shuts down, can you still open past work? (Local files: always)
!
Cloud tools: model locked to one vendor — no agent swapping, no self-hosting, no BYOK.
✓
Can you audit the code line by line? (Apache-2.0, fully open — fork, self-host, commercial use all allowed)
!
Cloud tools: can you export your preference and memory data — and truly delete it?
